summary_paragraph: A woman with metastatic breast cancer and a history of gastroparesis was readmitted three days after discharge due to recurrent nausea and vomiting. She had completed a course of vancomycin for C. difficile colitis and was found to be malnourished. A GJ tube was placed on hospital day two, and jejunal feeding was initiated to address nutritional needs and prevent refeeding syndrome. She tolerated tube feeds well, with gradual improvement in symptoms. Her medications were continued, except for holding Denosumab pending oncology follow-up. She was discharged home with services, on a regimen of continuous tube feeds, oral supplements, and home medications, with plans for outpatient follow-up in gastroenterology and oncology.
